chunks: A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the taste of water, so he said: 'Ask to understand, and do not ask to harass. The taste of water is the taste of life.'

key_terms.تَعَنُّت: Obstinate fault-finding; asking with intent to harass or embarrass rather than to learn
key_terms.تَفَقُّه: Seeking understanding/religious comprehension; asking with genuine intent to learn
key_terms.طَعْمُ الْحَيَاةِ: The taste of life; a metaphorical description of water as the essence of life

ai.seo_question: What is the taste of water according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the taste of water by an unnamed man. The Imam first rebuked the questioner's attitude, distinguishing between sincere inquiry for understanding (tafaqquh) and hostile questioning intended to irritate or find fault (ta'annut). He then offered a profound answer: water's taste is the taste of life itself, alluding to the essential and life-sustaining nature of water as acknowledged in Quranic cosmology.
